channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: 2027 Soulangh AiR Program
item.description: Soulangh Cultural Park occupies the buildings of the Jiali Sugar Factory, which opened in 1906 as the Meiji Sugar Corporation's first modern refinery and ran until 1995; award-winning Taiwanese architects converted its Japanese-era warehouses into a cultural park that opened to the public in 2005. Its artist-in-residence programme has run since 2013 and is open to all artistic disciplines, worldwide. The 2027 theme asks artists to reinterpret the stories of Tainan through sugar, salt or local cultural heritage - Jiali District sits at the geographical centre of Tainan's Saline Land, was an essential place of habitation for the Siraya people, and is still rich in Taoist temples and centipede parades. Residents need to be able to do field research and to plan and manage their own project, and are encouraged to work with the park's environment, including outdoor pieces. Each artist gets an accommodation suite with utilities included, a bicycle, an exhibition space fitted with lighting rails, wooden partitions and air conditioning, a shared studio, and free use of the park's projectors, monitors, speakers, lights and hardware tools. The funding comes in three parts: living expenses of up to NT$800 per day for up to 90 days (NT$72,000), an exhibition production fee of up to NT$200 per day for up to 90 days (NT$18,000), and a production budget of NT$150,000 covering exhibit materials, woodwork, painting and printing, 500 flyers, translation, artwork insurance, an opening press conference and workshop materials. Amounts are set by the review committee and are subject to 6-20 per cent withholding tax for foreign artists, who also pay a stamp duty of 0.1 per cent of the grant in cash. In return each resident stages one achievement exhibition and at least one parent-child workshop or open studio day before the residency ends, and files a report. Applicants need basic English or Chinese, a residency project plan, a CV and at least one recommendation letter carrying a handwritten signature. Copyright in the work stays with the artist, though the park may exhibit and publish it for educational and promotional purposes. The residency period runs 1 March to 30 October 2027 and applicants select three preferred terms; artists who do not stay for at least two-thirds of their term are disqualified. Applications go through the Tainan City Government's AIR in Tainan portal and results are announced in November 2026. — Deadline: September 10, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Residency + NT$72,000 grant + NT$150,000 production budget.

item.title: FULL CIRCLE · PARC Art Gallery
item.description: PARC Art Gallery is the nonprofit gallery inside the Plymouth Arts & Recreation Complex in Michigan, a building shared by more than thirty independent arts, education and recreation organisations. It is directed and curated by Élevé Art Gallery and is open to the public seven days a week, 10am to 8pm. FULL CIRCLE asks for original 2D and 3D work about cycles, connection and return: the seasons, growth, repetition and the passage of time; relationships, community and the ways people and places are linked; coming back to a person, place, memory or tradition; circles, rings, spirals and spheres as visual form; and ideas of completion, balance and wholeness. The gallery calls these starting points rather than requirements, and says it is drawn to work that invites viewers to look twice - to notice a pattern, connection or relationship that is not immediately apparent. Photography is named in the gallery's own list of eligible original media, alongside painting, drawing, sculpture, mixed media and original digital illustration, and photographs are specifically exempted from the ban on prints; giclee and fine-art reproductions of an existing painting, drawing or photograph are not eligible, and no AI-generated work of any kind is accepted. Entry is $35, non-refundable, for one to three pieces. Work must be original, independently completed without instruction, previously unshown at PARC, offered for sale, dry and finished, and suitable for all ages - the gallery serves visitors from toddlers upward and reserves the discretion to decline submissions on that basis. 2D work must hang on a wire (no plastic-covered wires, clips or sawtooth hangers), be professionally framed or have finished edges, and stay within 60 inches wide and 40lbs; 3D work must be freestanding, no taller than 40 inches and no heavier than 100lbs. Open to artists 18 and over who live or work in Michigan, with artists from elsewhere considered case by case provided the work can be dropped off and collected in person; if shipping is the only option the artist pays all costs. Notifications go out 6 September, drop-off is 8 September from 10am to noon, and the exhibition runs 10 September to 1 November 2026. — Deadline: September 4, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: Adler Gallery Exhibition — January–February 2027 · Port Washington Public Library
item.description: The Karen and Ed Adler Gallery at Port Washington Public Library gives one artist at a time a two-month solo exhibition in a dedicated gallery space, and there is an opening in the schedule for January-February 2027. Submissions are read by the library's Art Advisory Council: a preview committee makes the first cut and the full council then votes on whether to extend an invitation, with preview meetings held three times a year. During the run the artist is offered a two-hour public reception to talk about the work. Entry is free. Applicants fill in the library's own request form with a current resume and ten high-quality images of individual works, each labelled by title in the filename, tightly cropped so only the artwork shows, with no borders or backgrounds, and photographed straight on rather than at an angle; an image list giving title, medium and dimensions for each work is asked for, and a bio or promotional material can be attached as optional additional information. The library asks for a cohesive selection that reads as a curated exhibit rather than a survey. Only artists currently living in the tri-state area - New York, New Jersey and Connecticut - will be considered. Photography is part of the gallery's programme: past Adler Gallery shows include Steve Lampasona's The Light and Textures of New York City, a Holocaust survivor photography exhibit mounted around International Holocaust Remembrance Day, and Alan Richards's Let Me Show You Something, which built on archival and vintage photographs enhanced with drawing and digital painting. The exhibition runs 29 December 2026 to 28 February 2027. — Deadline: October 9, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Two-month solo exhibition.

item.title: Homage | The Americans · Griffin Museum of Photography
item.description: Part of the Griffin Museum's State of Our Union series, this online exhibition pays homage to Robert Frank, who crossed the country in 1958 with a camera and a Guggenheim and came back with a book that changed the way America saw itself. The museum describes The Americans as controversial and unflattering, a stark look at post-war America and a mirror the country did not know it needed - diners and gas stations, funerals and flags, jukeboxes and segregated buses. This call places Frank's original vision in dialogue with photographers working today who have inherited his instinct: the drive to look past the myth of the country and toward the lived reality of it. The museum invites photographers everywhere to contribute new work in direct homage to The Americans - images carrying forward Frank's willingness to look honestly, his eye for the overlooked corner and the unguarded face, and his belief that a nation is best understood not through its monuments but through its people. Entrants are asked to send their homage to Frank, their vision of America, and to say how Frank inspired them as a photographer. The online exhibition runs October 1 to 30, 2026. It sits in the Griffin Museum's 2026 Online Exhibition Program, which puts out a new open call each quarter on themes drawn from the museum's own exhibition schedule. Entry is free, global and open to anyone - the museum states plainly that 'our online exhibitions are always free of entry, global and open'. Submissions go through a Google Form; files must be sRGB JPGs sized between 1200 and 2000 pixels on the longest side and under 1.2 MB, or they are disqualified. Work is reviewed by the museum's in-house curatorial team with final selection by Executive Director Crista Dix. Recent online calls have drawn between 200 and 400 entries. Online exhibitions run one to one-and-a-half months; selected artists get a social media package ahead of the opening, and some shows generate guest-juror Critic's Picks or artist Q&As. Copyright stays with the artist throughout. — Deadline: September 25, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: To the Sea · Griffin Museum of Photography
item.description: The Griffin Museum wants photographs of water in all its moods - a wave breaking, the horizon at sunset, fog rolling over the harbour, a quiet cove, a storm coming in. The museum frames the theme around a pull that is older than any of us: summers at the beach, winter walks in the sand, storm waves against the shore, and the stories about what lies beneath the tideline that have filled imaginations for generations with monsters, demons and sirens just past what we can see. To the Sea is an invitation to capture that connection, whether from the shoreline, a pier, or simply watching the tide come in - every photograph a small piece of a much older story about why, no matter how far we wander, we always find our way back to the water's edge. The online exhibition runs 5 October 2026 to 1 January 2027, the longest of the museum's current online shows. It sits in the Griffin Museum's 2026 Online Exhibition Program, which puts out a new open call each quarter on themes drawn from the museum's own exhibition schedule. item.title: Earth, Wind & Fire · Griffin Museum of Photography
item.description: Long before they were a force in music, earth, wind and fire were forces of nature - and the Griffin Museum wants photographs that find them at work in the American landscape. Wind moving through tall grass or across a mountain ridge; fire as the warmth of a sunset, the glow of golden hour, the last light before dusk; earth in the shape of every hill, canyon and shoreline built up over centuries. The museum points to the deserts of the Southwest, the wheat fields of the Midwest, the granite coast of New England and the wide open sky of the plains, and asks for work that celebrates the elemental beauty of a country these forces are still shaping - fog lifting off a New England mountain at dawn, sunlight breaking through storm clouds over open farmland, the textures of stone, sand and soil under changing American light. The call is part of the museum's State of Our Union series and the online exhibition runs November 1 to 30, 2026. It sits in the Griffin Museum's 2026 Online Exhibition Program, which puts out a new open call each quarter on themes drawn from the museum's own exhibition schedule. Entry is free, global and open to anyone - the museum states plainly that 'our online exhibitions are always free of entry, global and open'.
